summary: Iteration 8 — Full validation of NEW features (UTC↔IST TZ toggle, Usage History page + filters + CSV export + sortable columns, Kill checkout via lmremove, Feature Detail modal on ServerDetail, sortable headers on Dashboard/Expiry/Usage). Backend: 24/24 new iteration-8 tests PASS + 21/21 iteration-7 regression PASS = 45/45 (100%). Frontend: 13/13 critical UI flows verified via Playwright on live preview URL — TZ flips IST↔UTC↔IST correctly, Usage page renders with 7 preset buttons + 7 sortable headers + correct /api/usage/export anchor, Dashboard CheckoutTable shows 7 sortable headers + 82 kill buttons (admin), Expiry page 8 sortable headers, ServerDetail shows 5 clickable feature rows that open the feature-detail-modal with kill buttons, Checkouts tab shows 14 detail-kill buttons. Mock-mode kill returns ok:true exec.mode='mock'. Engineer role correctly receives 403. usage_history upsert is idempotent — no duplicate explosion on repeated /api/checkouts. CSV header matches spec exactly. No bugs found.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 2242 lines (was 1968 in iter7) — well over the 700-line guideline. Splitting into auth.py, usage.py, crypto.py, scheduler.py, options_validator.py, csv_exports.py becomes urgent before iter9.

kill_checkout (server.py:1332-1364) does NOT validate the `feature`, `user`, or `host` payload values against any allow-list / regex — these strings get directly interpolated into a shell command (`lmremove -h {feature} {vendor_daemon} {host} {user}`). In SSH adapter mode this is a shell-injection vector if any of those fields contains a space, semicolon, backtick, or `$()`. Recommend shlex.quote() each user-supplied value or validate against /^[A-Za-z0-9._@:-]+$/ before composing the command.

usage_history TTL index uses BSON Date field `last_seen` (good) but the DB query / sort path uses `last_seen_iso` (string). Mixing two timestamp representations in one collection invites subtle bugs — pick one. The sort on the string ISO works only because ISO-8601 strings sort lexicographically.

_build_usage_query (server.py:1926-1947) anchors user/feature regex with ^ and $ but the `vendor` filter is exact-match (no anchoring). Slight inconsistency — vendor case-sensitivity will trip up admins.
/api/usage/export builds the full CSV in memory via StringIO. With 10k+ rows + USAGE_TTL_DAYS=365 this could allocate megabytes. Wrap in StreamingResponse like is recommended for /api/expiry/export.

/api/usage (GET) is NOT gated by require_admin — any authenticated engineer can pull the full usage history including PIDs and host names. Consider whether engineer role should see only their own sessions, or admin-only.
/api/usage/facets (GET) shares the same exposure — non-admin engineers can enumerate every user/host/server name. Tighten if needed.
